characteristics.name: Study name
characteristics.value: Routine versus clinically indicated replacement of peripheral intravenous catheters in elderly people: a multicenter randomized controlled equivalence trial

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value:
Study design: Multicenter randomized controlled equivalence trial 

Method of Randomisation: randomly assigned (scratch card) in a 1:1 ratio

Concealment of allocation: Not blinded

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Inclusion criteria: 1.Aged 60 years or over; 2.Peripheral intravenous catheter in situ with expected therapy >4 days; 3.The venous treatment has not started; 4.The patients has normal mind, clear speech and cooperative behavior; 5.Voluntary subjects, signing informed consent and good compliance. 

Exclusion criteria: 1.Patients who need 2 or more needles at the same time; 2.Patients with catheter-related blood steam infections; 3.Planned removal of catheter <= 24 hours; 4.Catheter already in situ >72 hours; 5.Individuals with immunodeficiency diseases or receiving immunosuppressive therapy; 6.Peripheral venous catheter placement in the emergency department or operating room.

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Intervention group: Daily researchers will evaluate and register the catheter. For patients with tube drawing will be recorded the causes of remove the tube in detail, such as shedding, infiltration, etc. Evaluation continued until 48h after remove the indwelling needle. Extubation is based on clinical indications.

Control group: Routine replacement of peripheral intravenous catheters

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value: Primary Outcomes: 1. Phlebitis, 2. Infiltration, 3. Occlusion, 4. Catheter related bloodstream infection, 5. Cost, 6. Catheters per patient
